story: UPDATE on DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC's proposed underwater AI data center and tidal array, FERC Project P-15423, with runner-up Kenai Peninsula Borough Ordinance 2026-35 on weather modification

claims.claim: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC's application to FERC describes a 100.0 MW integrated tidal energy and subsea data center facility in Upper Cook Inlet, in the Nikiski and East Forelands corridor.
claims.verbatim: The proposed project consists of a 100.0 MW integrated tidal energy and subsea data center facility located in the Upper Cook Inlet, specifically within the Nikiski / East Forelands Corridor.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, application to FERC
claims.notes: Background fact about the record (filed before the window). Read from the eLibrary file download, text at out/2026-10-22/ferc/20260211-5060.txt (cover letter to Secretary Reese). Exhibit 1 and the draft notice repeat 100.0 MW. Corroborated by FERC's September 1st notice (20260901-3051) and the Federal Register text of that notice (91 FR, September 4th). The applicant's address is Needham, Massachusetts and the filing is signed by Louis Wolfson, Managing Member.

claims.claim: The application proposes about 330 to 350 marine hydrokinetic turbines.
claims.verbatim: Turbine Array: ~330-350 Marine Hydrokinetic (MHK) turbines.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, application to FERC
claims.notes: Read from the eLibrary file download, text at out/2026-10-22/ferc/20260211-5060.txt (Exhibit 1). The original has an en dash between 330 and 350, changed to a hyphen here to meet the house dash rule. FERC's September 1st notice repeats 'approximately 330-350 marine hydrokinetic turbines'.

claims.claim: The application proposes 66 modular pressure-vessel Hives that hold AI compute racks and are cooled by passive subsea immersion cooling.
claims.verbatim: 66 modular pressure-vessel "Hives" housing AI-compute racks, co-located within the array to utilize direct-coupled power and passive subsea immersion cooling.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, application to FERC
claims.notes: Read from the eLibrary file download, text at out/2026-10-22/ferc/20260211-5060.txt (Exhibit 1). FERC's notice calls them '66 modular subsea-compute hives (data center pods)'.

claims.claim: The application proposes a cable of about 3.5 miles, rated 115 kV, carrying both power and fiber optics from the hub to shore.
claims.verbatim: A ~3.5-mile, 115kV hybrid power/fiber-optic armored cable connecting the Hub to the shore.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, application to FERC
claims.notes: Read from the eLibrary file download, text at out/2026-10-22/ferc/20260211-5060.txt (Exhibit 1, section 3). The same verbatim supports 115 kV, which can be a second value anchor. FERC's notice repeats 'an approximately 3.5-mile long, 115 kV hybrid power/fiber-optic armored subsea cable'.

claims.claim: The application targets a cable landing on the Nikiski Industrial Corridor shoreline between the Agrium Kenai Nitrogen Operations and the Kenai LNG Plant.
claims.verbatim: specifically targeting the shoreline between the Agrium Kenai Nitrogen Operations and the Kenai LNG Plant.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, application to FERC
claims.notes: Read from the eLibrary file download, text at out/2026-10-22/ferc/20260211-5060.txt. The word 'Nutrien' does NOT appear in the application. The Kenai Peninsula Borough's motion (20260914-5074) calls the site the 'Kenai Nutrien Operations Facility'. If the deck says Nutrien, that is an editorial gloss and this claim doesn't support it.

claims.claim: Exhibit 3 of the application says the project boundary encloses about 1,400 to 1,650 acres centered on the deep-water Cook Inlet thalweg.
claims.verbatim: The project boundary encloses a corridor of approximately 1,400 to 1,650 acres centered in the deep-water Cook Inlet Thalweg.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, application to FERC
claims.notes: Read from the eLibrary file download, text at out/2026-10-22/ferc/20260211-5060.txt. The cover letter and draft notice give a single figure, 'approximately 1,650 acres'. As a sanity check I ran the shoelace formula on the four Exhibit 3 corners (C07), using a flat approximation at 60.73 degrees N, and got about 6.9 square km, roughly 1,700 acres. That matches the top of the stated range. The long side of the polygon is about 3.5 miles.

claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, application to FERC
claims.notes: Read from the eLibrary file download, text at out/2026-10-22/ferc/20260211-5060.txt. The coordinates sit in a table. The extracted text puts one cell per line, and the verbatim joins those cells with single spaces. Datum WGS84. The corners are NW, NE, SE and SW in that order. They are good for a map slide.

claims.notes: This claim is about an ABSENCE, so no page string can prove it directly. The verbatim is the docket's most recent intervention, quoted as a boundary marker. Method: I read every one of the 135 entries in the showrunner's listing (out/2026-10-22/ferc/filings.json, retrieved through FERC's eLibrary search API at 2026-10-23T06:20Z, which is October 22nd, 22:20 Alaska time), covering descriptions and author affiliations. None names CIRI, Cook Inlet Region or Kenaitze. This tells us nothing about their views, and it is not proof that DeepGreen never contacted them. State it only as 'no filing listed as of' the retrieval time.

claims.claim: The Kenai Peninsula Borough Assembly enacted Ordinance 2026-35, as amended, on October 20th.
claims.verbatim: ENACTED BY THE ASSEMBLY OF THE KENAI PENINSULA BOROUGH THIS 20TH DAY OF OCTOBER, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough, Ordinance 2026-35 (signed)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. The signed ordinance is attachment 'Ordinance 2026-35' on Legistar matter 32039, signed by Assembly President Ryan Tunseth and attested by Borough Clerk Michele Turner. The Legistar histories endpoint (webapi.legistar.com/v1/kpb/matters/32039/histories) records an action on 2026-10-20 by the Assembly, 'enacted as amended', on a motion by Truesdell, after an amendment by Niesen. The matter record itself still showed MatterStatusName 'Public Hearing' and null MatterPassedDate, MatterEnactmentDate and MatterEnactmentNumber (last modified 2026-10-21 UTC). That's a lag in the record, so don't cite those fields. KDLL (October 21st) and Alaska Public Media (October 22nd, the same KDLL story) agree.

claims.claim: The assembly vote on Ordinance 2026-35 was 7 yes, 0 no, with 2 members absent.
claims.verbatim: Vote: 7 Yes, 0 No, 2 Absent
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough, Ordinance 2026-35 (signed)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. The page 2 roll call reads 'Yes: Berga, Cooper, Ecklund, Eicher, Niesen, Truesdell, Tunseth; No: None; Absent: Dunne, Hibbert'. Neither KDLL nor Alaska Public reported a count.

claims.claim: Ordinance 2026-35 adds a new borough code section, KPB 17.10.165, on weather modification and geoengineering on borough lands, introduced by the mayor and assembly member Lenora Niesen.
claims.verbatim: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING BOROUGH CODE TO ENACT A NEW SECTION, KPB 17.10.165, RELATED TO WEATHER MODIFICATION AND GEOENGINEERING ACTIVITIES ON BOROUGH LANDS
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough, Ordinance 2026-35 (signed)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. The header reads 'Introduced by: Mayor, Niesen', introduced September 15th, hearing October 20th. Legistar MatterIntroDate is 2026-09-03, which is probably the agenda-entry date. The history shows introduction at the September 15th Assembly meeting.

claims.claim: The ordinance requires an application for a borough commercial lease or land use permit for weather modification to state the intended outcome and list the chemicals, flares, flight frequency and release coordinates.
claims.verbatim: must identify the intended outcome of the proposed activity and include in the application the following: (1) Type of chemicals that will be used to attempt weather modification
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough, Ordinance 2026-35 (signed)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. The ten items cover chemical type, chemical quantity, flare details including serial numbers and weight, total pyrotechnic material, MSDS, frequency, duration and altitude of flights, total duration, maximum flights, and release coordinates with predicted impact areas. KDLL's summary agrees.

claims.claim: The ordinance prohibits geoengineering and weather modification on borough lands open for casual use.
claims.verbatim: Geoengineering or weather modification activities are prohibited on borough lands open for casual use.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough, Ordinance 2026-35 (signed)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. KDLL gives examples of casual use, 'like berry-picking or skiing'. The ordinance defines the terms as including cloud seeding, solar radiation modification and stratospheric aerosol injection.

claims.claim: Failing to file the required closeout information carries a $1,000 per day fine and a 5-year ban on applying for a commercial lease or land use permit.
claims.verbatim: subject to a $1000 per day fine for each day the closeout information is not provided and a 5-year ban on applying for a commercial leas or commercial land use permit.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough, Ordinance 2026-35 (signed)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. The verbatim keeps the ordinance's own typo 'commercial leas'. KDLL reported no penalties, so this detail comes only from the primary document. The amendment that was adopted is a separate attachment ('LAYDOWN Niesen Amendment') that I didn't read. The signed text is marked 'Enacted as Amended', so I take it as the final text.

claims.claim: Ordinance 2026-35 took effect immediately.
claims.verbatim: This ordinance shall be effective immediately.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough, Ordinance 2026-35 (signed)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. Section 4. KDLL also reports 'The new section of code is effective immediately.'

claims.claim: Mayor Peter Micciche told KDLL the borough's ability to limit weather modification and geoengineering is limited to borough lands for now.
claims.verbatim: "Our ability to limit weather modification and geoengineering is limited to borough lands at this point," he said.
claims.source_outlet: KDLL (Ashlyn O'Hara)
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP, IN WINDOW. The verbatim quote is on the fetched page. Alaska Public Media republished the story on October 22nd with the same quote, but that isn't an independent source. The ordinance's scope, borough lands only, independently supports the substance.

claims.claim: Rainmaker's own report says its drones released 19 flares carrying about 374.3 grams of silver iodide over the Kenai Peninsula on August 23rd.
claims.verbatim: 19 red flares were released by drones EL-151 and EL-153
claims.source_outlet: Rainmaker Technology Corporation, validation report
claims.suggested_hedge: according to Rainmaker's own report
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP background, before the window. This is the company's self-report. A second verbatim on the same page supports the 374.3 g: 'for a total of approximately 374.3 g of AgI', at roughly 19.7 g per flare (19.7 times 19 is 374.3, which checks). The date verbatim is 'in the Kenai Peninsula, AK on August 23, 2026'. The report has seven seeding signatures, missions 4 to 7 used two flares each, and flares totaled 4+4+3+2+2+2+2 = 19, which checks. The report doesn't name Homer, but KDLL says the work was 'tested in Homer'.

claims.claim: Rainmaker's report estimates seeding produced a mean of 57.62 acre-feet of precipitation, a modeled figure from radar rather than a gauge measurement.
claims.verbatim: the mean precipitation volume attributed to seeding was 57.62 acre-feet
claims.source_outlet: Rainmaker Technology Corporation, validation report
claims.suggested_hedge: Rainmaker estimates, from radar modeling,
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. The figure is MODELED. It comes from radar reflectivity converted through a 27-member ensemble of Z-S relationships, the report gives a 5th to 95th percentile range of 41.70 to 89.35 acre-feet, and no ground gauge measurement is described. KDLL separately reports 'roughly one-hundredth of an inch of precipitation over the project area'.

claims.claim: KDLL reported that Alaska's Department of Natural Resources said cloud seeding is not addressed in state law and that it did not give Rainmaker permission.
claims.verbatim: that activity is not addressed in state law.
claims.source_outlet: KDLL (Ashlyn O'Hara)
claims.suggested_hedge: according to KDLL
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP, IN WINDOW. Only this fragment was returned verbatim, and the attribution to DNR comes from the fetch summary. For balance, KDLL also reports that Rainmaker CEO Augustus Doricko said the company 'received all applicable permits and permissions for its cloud-seeding operation'. Legistar matter 32039 lists a 'Letter from State of Alaska' attachment that I didn't read.

killed.claim: DeepGreen's Eastport, Maine twin project is up to 15 MW with up to 50 turbines (Boston Globe, October 13th).
killed.why: Disputed. FERC's Federal Register notice for P-15424 (91 FR 54868, August 25th) describes 'up to 16 marine hydrokinetic turbine-generator units, each rated at 300-kilowatt', which comes to 4.8 MW. The Eastport City Council's September 22nd letter reads the notice the same way and adds 34 compute pods. The Globe page has no byline or date. Use C50 and C51.
